name: Federal Reserve
mandate: Dual mandate: stable prices and maximum employment
islm_text: The policy rate barely moved, so the LM curve stays roughly where it was; changes in output now come mainly from the IS side (fiscal policy, exports, confidence). With a real rate of +0.1% against an assumed neutral of about 0.75%, policy is accommodative: it is still pushing demand up.
currency_text: US rates are -1.13 pp versus the average of the other major central banks. The dollar has barely moved on average against their currencies over 12 months. Because the dollar is the world's reserve currency, Fed moves spill over into every other economy's financing costs and exchange rate. The exchange rate has been fairly stable, so its effect on inflation is small.

inflation.text: Inflation is 3.7%, above target (2% (PCE measure; CPI shown here)). Pushing it up: loose real rates. Over the next 12–18 months the rules point to inflation rising further above target.

name: People's Bank of China
mandate: Price stability, growth, employment and financial stability (multiple goals)
islm_text: The policy rate barely moved, so the LM curve stays roughly where it was; changes in output now come mainly from the IS side (fiscal policy, exports, confidence). With a real rate of +2.3% against an assumed neutral of about 1%, policy is restrictive: it is still holding demand back.
currency_text: PBoC rates are -0.88 pp versus the Fed. The CNY has strengthened 6.5% against the USD over 12 months. A stronger currency makes imports cheaper, which pulls inflation down.

inflation.text: Inflation is 0.7%, below target (around 2% (government CPI goal)). Pushing inflation down: restrictive real rates, a stronger currency. Over the next 12–18 months the rules point to inflation falling further below target (watch for deflation risk).

name: European Central Bank
mandate: Price stability in the euro area
islm_text: The policy rate rose 0.50 pp in 12 months, so the LM curve shifts up/left: money is tighter, borrowing costs rise, investment and spending cool. The new equilibrium has a higher interest rate (r) and lower output (Y). With a real rate of -1.5% against an assumed neutral of about 0.25%, policy is accommodative: it is still pushing demand up.
currency_text: ECB rates are -1.38 pp versus the Fed. Over the year the gap moved 0.50 pp in the EUR's favour, which tends to attract capital and support the EUR (Mundell-Fleming). The EUR has weakened 3.7% against the USD over 12 months. A weaker currency makes imports dearer, adding imported inflation.

inflation.text: Inflation is 4.0%, above target (2%, symmetric). Pushing inflation down: rate hikes over the past year. Pushing it up: loose real rates, a weaker currency (imported inflation). Over the next 12–18 months the rules point to inflation rising further above target.

name: Bank of Japan
islm_text: The policy rate rose 0.75 pp in 12 months, so the LM curve shifts up/left: money is tighter, borrowing costs rise, investment and spending cool. The new equilibrium has a higher interest rate (r) and lower output (Y). With a real rate of -0.8% against an assumed neutral of about 0%, policy is accommodative: it is still pushing demand up.
currency_text: BoJ rates are -2.62 pp versus the Fed. Over the year the gap moved 0.76 pp in the JPY's favour, which tends to attract capital and support the JPY (Mundell-Fleming). The JPY has weakened 4.1% against the USD over 12 months. A weaker currency makes imports dearer, adding imported inflation.

inflation.text: Inflation is 2.1%, close to target (2%). Pushing inflation down: rate hikes over the past year. Pushing it up: loose real rates, a weaker currency (imported inflation). Over the next 12–18 months the rules point to inflation drifting up.

name: Bank of England
mandate: Price stability, then support for government economic policy
stance_note: cuts paused in the last 3 months
islm_text: The policy rate fell 0.25 pp in 12 months, so the LM curve shifts down/right: money is looser, borrowing is cheaper, investment and spending pick up. The new equilibrium has a lower interest rate (r) and higher output (Y). With a real rate of +0.1% against an assumed neutral of about 0.5%, policy is neutral: it is neither braking nor boosting demand much.
currency_text: BoE rates are -0.12 pp versus the Fed. The GBP has barely moved against the USD over 12 months. The exchange rate has been fairly stable, so its effect on inflation is small.

inflation.text: Inflation is 3.6%, above target (2%). Pushing it up: rate cuts over the past year. Over the next 12–18 months the rules point to inflation staying roughly where it is.
